children: Infosys’ expanded Indore centre will support AI, cloud, application development and cybersecurity capabilities

IT firm Infosys has expanded its development centre in Indore with a new 3,30,000-square-foot software development block, as the Indian IT services company seeks to deepen its presence in Central India and tap the region's technology talent pool.

The new Software Development Block-2 (SDB-2) was inaugurated at Infosys' campus in Indore's Super Corridor in the presence of Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, Indore Member of Parliament Shankar Lalwani and state legislator Manoj Nirbhay Singh Patel, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.
Infosys' Indore centre currently employs more than 3,300 people and serves clients globally across banking, financial services and insurance, retail, life sciences and manufacturing.
The expansion will strengthen the company's capabilities in cloud, application development, artificial intelligence and machine learning, and cybersecurity, Infosys said.

The move comes as IT services companies expand delivery capacity around India's major and emerging technology hubs to access engineering talent beyond traditional centres such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune.

Infosys also plans to increase its engagement with Madhya Pradesh's academic and technology ecosystem through skilling initiatives and institutional partnerships, including with IIT Indore, IIM Indore and Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya.

The new facility incorporates energy-efficient systems and features such as low-energy cooling, smart building automation, rainwater harvesting and wastewater recycling, the company said. It will also include flexible workstations, training facilities and wellness centres.

"Indore is steadily emerging as an important technology hub, supported by a strong talent base and a growing innovation ecosystem," Yadav said, adding that Infosys' investment would create employment opportunities for skilled youth in the state.
Infosys Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said the expansion would help the company leverage the region's talent pool and strengthen its AI, cloud and digital technology capabilities.
